classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the plotted curve as decreasing and connect that behaviour to the candidate base between zero and one.

inlines.text: Which is a possible value of

spec.description: Square grid with one-unit minor lines and two-unit major lines, two-ended black axes, selected numeric labels and italic axis letters. A decreasing green logarithmic curve has no endpoint arrows or point markers. Green replaces source teal using the standard palette.
spec.mathematics: Analytic curve y=ln(x)/ln(2/3), clipped to -5<=x<=15 and -10<=y<=10. The curve crosses (1,0), decreases and is concave up.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve is visible. Its base is not labelled; the selected base and explanation remain in answer fields.

answer.worked: A logarithmic curve is decreasing when $0<a<1$. Since $0<\frac23<1$ and $\frac32>1$, the possible base is $a=\frac23$.
